FLAG: length-implausible: straight-line Abu Qurqas(town)-to-Asyut(city) is ~89.9 km vs stated 135.00 km, ratio ~1.50 -- exceeds the brief's ~1.4x caution threshold, matching the brief's own stated concern. Notably GEM's EXISTING P6700 (the first-phase 'Abu Qurqas-Asyut Gas pipeline' this row duplicates) shows an even larger overshoot: 150km stated vs the same ~90km straight line, ratio ~1.67. Both the original and the duplicate line show a similar large detour ratio, which argues against a simple wrong-endpoint error on P8056 specifically (a wrong endpoint would be unlikely to reproduce almost the same ratio as its sibling) and instead points to either (a) a genuinely circuitous west-bank corridor, or (b) a systematic issue with how this segment family's lengths are recorded in GEM. Flagging both for a human route-drafter's attention; not resolved here.  FLAG: first-phase-exists:P6700 -- GEM already has 'South Valley Gas Pipeline / Abu Qurqas-Asyut Gas pipeline' (P6700, operating, 150km) under the SAME PipelineName, confirming P8056 ('...II', construction, 135km) is the announced parallel/duplicate line, not a duplicate database entry. The two should be cross-referenced (e.g. via RouteNotes) but are legitimately separate rows.  FLAG: sibling-length-anomaly (out of scope, flagging for awareness): P6699 'Beni Suef-Abu Qurqas Gas pipeline' and P6700 'Abu Qurqas-Asyut Gas pipeline' both carry LengthKnownKm=150.00 exactly -- an identical value for two different named segments, which reads as a possible copy/data-entry artifact in GEM's existing data rather than coincidence. Neither is one of my assigned PIDs; surfacing for the QC team.
